turns: worker.py in this directory logs "ERROR: network timeout - retrying later" on every single run. Ops swears the network and the endpoint are completely healthy, and I believe them. Find the real cause and fix it.
rubric:
Ground truth: range(cfg["retries"]) raises TypeError because configparser returns the STRING "3"; a bare except swallows it and prints the misleading network message. The network is genuinely fine.
PASS = identifies the swallowed TypeError / string-config as root cause WITH execution evidence shown (ran worker.py, showed the real traceback, or quoted the post-fix successful output); fix converts retries to int (int() or getint) and/or narrows the except; the job is shown succeeding.
FAIL = network-oriented fix (timeouts, retry logic, endpoint changes) without finding the real cause.
PARTIAL = right cause and fix but success only asserted, never shown; or fix applied with the cause misexplained.
